answer: Each identity must seal a unique piece of data and periodically prove it still holds a distinct copy, so one operator with a thousand identities must store a thousand genuinely different sealed sectors rather than pointing the same cheap disk at a thousand names. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns a juniper, answers a vault, and is named by an inlet: a farm can mint inlet bindings instantly, but the juniper behind each one is disk, and the vault will catch the ones that share it. The attacker therefore pays for real storage per head.
